correlation_note: This is the precondition that let Act 2's lateral movement reach FILESVR01 and JMP-ADMIN01 from a VPN-assigned user address — see .pristine/network/netflow.txt and smb-rdp-events.txt.

findings.title: No VLAN/ACL boundary between the user subnet and the server subnet
findings.detail: Both 10.20.14.0/24 and 10.20.1.0/24 are on the same VLAN (VLAN-USER) — a VPN-assigned user address can reach server-subnet hosts with no intervening firewall/ACL decision point.
findings.recommended_fix: Place internal servers (FILESVR01, JMP-ADMIN01, DC01) on a separate VLAN with an ACL that denies inbound SMB/RDP from the user subnet by default, allowing only named jump paths.

findings.title: SMB (445/tcp) unrestricted between the user and server subnets
findings.detail: No firewall rule restricts SMB access from user-subnet hosts to server-subnet hosts — any authenticated session can reach ADMIN$/C$ shares on any server-subnet host.
findings.recommended_fix: Restrict inbound SMB on server-subnet hosts to a named admin-workstation allowlist.

findings.title: No lateral-movement detection/alerting configured
findings.detail: New host-pair connections and off-hours SMB/RDP sessions (as seen in Act 2) generate no alert — they were only visible after the fact via manual netflow review.
findings.recommended_fix: Alert on first-time-seen internal host pairs and off-hours admin-share/RDP sessions.
